html:
SMTO-TSK-0004 — This command doesn't fit the task's current state

GUID: e8e1c656-6388-401a-9dd9-bda3ce07787a
Slug: task-command-conflict
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The command you used, such as /stop, /pause or /resume, doesn't apply right now. The task may have finished already, been replaced by a newer attempt, or not be in a state that allows it. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and look at the task's current status in the conversation. The status shows whether the task is running, paused or finished, which decides which commands work.
  2. Use a command that fits: /stop only while a task is active, /pause only while it is working, and /resume only when it is paused. Each command checks the task's state and refuses when it doesn't apply, such as stopping a task that already ended.
  3. If you switched or deleted conversations, open the conversation you meant and run the command there. Commands act on the selected conversation and its latest task, not an older attempt.

What success looks like

  • The command is accepted and the task's status changes as expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting which command you used and on which task. Don't keep resending the command from a page you haven't reloaded; it is checked against the task's latest status each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • CommandControlPlane rejected a slash or control command: no conversation or a deleted one, no run, a changed target, nothing active to stop, a pause already pending, or a run that cannot be paused, resumed or compacted.

What this means

  • CommandControlPlane raises its fixed-message CommandConflict when command scope, target identity or available control state fails validation. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • CommandControlPlane raises its fixed-message CommandConflict when command scope, target identity or available control state fails validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the command's specific catalog message and fresh target/control state rather than inferring one cause from the exception class.

How to fix it

  • CommandControlPlane.run_target and require_available in src/agent_runtime/commands/control_plane.py raise CommandConflict for no_conversation, conversation_changed, no_run, target_changed, no_active, pause_pending, cannot_pause, cannot_resume or cannot_compact. Refresh the task's current snapshot (status, resume_allowed, compact_allowed, continued_by) and submit an action that state allows.
  • Refresh current task control state and submit an action allowed for that state.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The command's scope and current target satisfy its advertised availability conditions.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
